This was the first game my mum beat all by herself (after giving her a tutorial as there is none in this game). I'd love to know if there were other match-up puzzle games that play differently than the usual (more like Gridland, less like Bejeweled and it's clones. She's played those).

I want to keep up this new positive relationship with games, but her preferred genre (match-making) are outside of my jurisdiction of gaming knowledge, so I don't know what's all available. She also loves word making games but the only ones I know that exist are child-level teaching games. She uses a PC, Windows 7.

Thank you and good luck to this subverse!

Bejeweled clones are usually called "Match 3" games. Here's one that has some combat mechanics, sort of like Grindland. (I didn't play very much of Gridland, but the fighty bit was familiar.)

There's a whole list of Match 3 games here sorted by rating if you want to try them out. I think the top rated one, Monsters and Dungeons, also has combat. This isn't my genre though.

Word making games? Like Scrabble? Or Hangman? Here's a hangman game, just released yesterday. It's simple, but I had some fun with that.

There are two routes that I try to take when I'm recommending a game to someone who doesn't play games. You can go with a variant on something familiar, like Minesweeper. Everyone's played Minesweeper, so a murder mystery game based on Minesweeper would be a pretty good choice, right?

Or play Z-Rox. I posted about it here, on a different sub for game recommendations (disclaimer: which I moderate), but I've found it to be a very accessible game while still being challenging. Though beating it may be out of reach - once it moves from keyboard symbols to random objects it gets really hard.

I don't worry about how difficult the game actually is.
